title: fix(spec): bound `scale` at the renderer ceiling of 100 (#18972)
body:
Fixes #18972

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

`FieldSchema.scale` was declared as any non-negative integer with no upper bound, while every
renderer that turns it into fraction digits hits a hard platform ceiling of 100. Both declarations
of `scale` in `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` now carry that ceiling, with a refusal that says
**why** — it names the two primitives, the `RangeError` and the legal maximum — so an author reads a
platform limit they can verify rather than a cap somebody chose.

Evidence below is measured on this branch at `2d62629edf`, base `origin/main` = `176b03582e`.

## The platform fact the bound rests on

There is no reusable decimal-digit ceiling constant in `packages/spec`, so the number is newly minted
here and its justification has to be the platform. Measured first-hand this round, node v22.22.2:

| probe | reading |
| :-- | :-- |
| `(1.5).toFixed(100)` | ok |
| `(1.5).toFixed(101)` | `RangeError: toFixed() digits argument must be between 0 and 100` |
| `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 100 })` | ok |
| `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 101 })` | `RangeError: maximumFractionDigits value is out of range.` |

The boundary is exactly 100, reproducing objectui#9808's reading rather than carrying it through. A
unit test re-measures both primitives on every run and asserts the schema's own accept/refuse
boundary sits on the same number, so the literal is never trusted on its own: if a future runtime
moves either limit, the pin goes red and the declaration is re-argued.

Corroboration from inside this repo: `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:994` already holds
`const MAX_FORMULA_SCALE = 100`, whose docblock reads "`FieldSchema.scale` is `z.number().int().min(0)`
with no upper bound, so an author CAN declare more — and a display-precision declaration must never be
the reason a read fails." That is the consumer-side half of this same fact, written as a defence. This
PR is the producer-side half. The two are deliberately not one import: `packages/spec` may not depend
on a consumer package, and the new constant is module-private so no published API surface moves.

## The dispatch's open question, answered: BOTH sites in this file are bounded

The file carries two `scale` declarations. The card names only `FieldSchema.scale`; whether the
grid-column one reaches the same renderers was left to be measured. It does, by a different primitive,
so both are bounded:

| declaration | the reader it reaches | primitive |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `InlineGridColumnSchema.scale` (`field.zod.ts:882` at the base) | objectui `computeRow`, `packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.tsx:322` — `next[c.name] = scale != null ? Number(v.toFixed(scale)) : v` | `toFixed` |
| `FieldSchema.scale` (`field.zod.ts:1158` at the base) | objectui number cell renderer, `packages/fields/src/index.tsx:747` — `maximumFractionDigits: scale ?? 20` | `Intl.NumberFormat` |

The link for the first row is not an inference: `InlineGridColumnSchema`'s own docblock declares it a
"STRICT mirror of the objectui inline-grid renderer's `GridColumn` (`packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.tsx`)",
and `GridColumn.scale` is the value `computeRow` hands to `toFixed`. Measured in the sibling checkout
`../objectui` at `dda8f3815d`. Two declarations, two renderers, one ceiling.

## Acceptance legs

**Subject.** `scale: 100` parses; `scale: 101` is refused at both sites with a `too_big` issue at
`[scale]` whose message names `toFixed`, `maximumFractionDigits`, `RangeError` and the legal maximum.

**Lit control (the same probe before the change).** At `176b03582e`, both sites answered `scale: 101`
with **PASS** — so this round demonstrably narrowed something, and the probe was never dead.

**Dark control.** `scale: -1` and `scale: 2.5` were refused before and are refused after, for the same
reasons, with the same codes and the same wording: `too_small` / "Too small: expected number to be >=0"
and `invalid_type` / "Invalid input: expected int, received number". The #8321 refusals are untouched;
only the top of the range moved.

**Zero-hit reading, with its radius.** Zero `scale` declarations above 100 exist in this repository —
`git grep` over all tracked files, 123 `scale: N` declarations as the lit control, 0 above 100. The
instrument's reachable radius is this repository's tracked file contents at `2d62629edf`. A known
target necessarily outside it: a `sys_metadata` row already stored in a running deployment's database,
which no in-repo instrument can read. Triage recorded the same blind spot on this card.

## What this PR deliberately does not touch

- **No renderer, no clamp, no fallback.** Refusing an unrenderable declaration at the door is this
  card; what a renderer should do when handed a large value is not, and stays objectui#9808's.
- **`CurrencyConfigSchema`'s alias table is untouched.** Its `scale` maps to `precision` on a different
  surface with its own bounds; the file's own comment says "do not conflate", and a pin asserts the
  currency config still accepts `precision: 10`.
- **`precision` is not bounded.** It is a total digit count and reaches neither primitive, so the
  renderer-ceiling argument does not carry to it. A pin records that the omission was measured rather
  than missed.
- **objectui is not changed** — read only, for the two renderer readings above.

## Verification

| command | result |
| :-- | :-- |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` | exit 0 — 492 files, 14490 tests passed |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/field.test.ts src/data/inline-related-columns.test.ts` | exit 0 — 284 tests passed |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` | exit 0 after `--fix` regenerated `content/docs/references/**` (`gen:docs`) — the two `scale` descriptions, nothing else |
| `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` | exit 0 — one declared-breaking changeset, disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` | exit 0 |
| gate families from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` | every command run, exit code captured before any pipe; see the report for the NOT MEASURED residue |

Seven of the derived gate commands could not measure anything in this container: they read built
`dist/` of packages this diff does not touch (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`,
`check:docs-transcript-drift`, `check:type-check-debt`, the two `@objectstack/lint` doc gates, and
`check:skill-examples`), and each exits with its own PREREQUISITE NOT MET verdict rather than a
finding. They are recorded as NOT MEASURED, not as green; CI builds the closure and runs them for real.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset` does not hold and no label is written: `@objectstack/spec` publishes `dist` in its
`files[]`, and this diff changes what that published artifact accepts at runtime. The changeset is a
`minor` carrying the **BREAKING** banner and the ADR-0087 disposition, per the launch-window
convention in which `major` is refused and breaking-ness rides the banner rather than the level.

## Acceptance notes

- **A third site, measured and deliberately left out of this diff.**
  `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:2768` (`FormFieldBaseSchema.scale`, the form-row override) carries
  the byte-identical unbounded declaration and reaches the same `Intl.NumberFormat` renderer — its own
  neighbouring comment states that objectui reads every one of these keys off the form row, copied onto
  the runtime field by `form-view.ts` `mapField` and plugin-form `sectionFields.ts`. The card records
  it as a reading it did **not** fold into its claim, and the dispatch's declared file surface is
  `field.zod.ts` only, so widening this diff to a second file would move a surface the claim does not
  name — the instrument this repo uses to keep parallel agents off each other's files. It is reported
  back for a decision rather than fixed silently; the fix is one line plus the shared constant, which
  would have to be promoted out of `field.zod.ts` at that point (a new export, so that PR declares
  clause ② `yes`).
- **noted, not filed: `precision` is bounded on one arm and unbounded on two others.**
  `CurrencyConfigSchema.precision` is `.max(10)`; `FieldSchema.precision` and
  `FormFieldBaseSchema.precision` have no maximum. No renderer-ceiling argument applies to any of them,
  and whether the three should agree is a judgement about three different field arms. Successor: the
  same seat that takes the `view.zod.ts` site above, since it is one line away from both.
- **noted, not filed: `MAX_FORMULA_SCALE` and this file's bound now record one platform fact twice.**
  Both are module-private and the dependency direction forbids sharing (`objectql` depends on `spec`,
  not the reverse), so the duplication is structural rather than an oversight. Successor: none today —
  it would take a shared constants entry point on the published surface, which is a wider decision than
  this card.
